openIssues.title: Harden the release-cadence workflow template (Copilot review findings from the 2026-07-13 apply batch)
openIssues.body:
Copilot code review on the five open release-cadence apply PRs (yourear#61, github-issue-triage-bot#169, ai-model-advisor#177, lounge-tv#22, votescot#128) surfaced five distinct findings — all against the shared template in `src/apply.js` (`buildReleaseCadenceWorkflow`), not against any one repo's copy. Eight repos carry this template (three merged 2026-07-13/14: repo-butler#322, bonnie-wee-plot#469, betis-escocia#468; the rest merging now), so the fix belongs here, once, with deployed copies reconciled afterwards — hand-patching individual PR branches would fork them away from the template and defeat the standard's uniformity.

## Findings

1. **Non-ancestor tag can cut an unintended release** (lounge-tv#22). `git rev-list --count "$tag..HEAD"` returns a large count when the latest release tag exists but is not an ancestor of the default-branch HEAD (e.g. tagged from a release branch). This is the only finding whose failure mode is a *wrong release* rather than a skip. Fix: guard with `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$tag" HEAD || skip`, fail closed.
2. **`gh api … 2>/dev/null || true` hides API errors as "No published release yet"** (yourear#61, votescot#128). Failure mode is a silent skip (fail-safe — no release is cut) but the log message is misleading and real outages are undiagnosable. Fix: let stderr through / distinguish error from empty while still skipping on error.
3. **`git rev-list … || echo 0` conflates resolution failure with "no commits"** (yourear#61, votescot#128). Same fail-safe-but-misleading shape as (2). Fix: handle the error path explicitly; only report "no commits" when the comparison succeeded.
4. **`--generate-notes` may need `pull-requests: read`** (ai-model-advisor#177). The `permissions:` block grants only `contents: write`; if note generation reads merged PRs, the first live run (1st/15th cron) could fail visibly. Verify and add `pull-requests: read` if needed.
5. **`actions/checkout@v4` is behind repo conventions** (ai-model-advisor#177 — its other workflows pin `@v6`). Decide a template-wide version (and pinning style) rather than per-repo drift.

## Risk assessment at merge time

Findings 2 and 3 only ever cause a *skip* (no release), matching the template's deliberate fail-safe design; 4 fails loudly and is recoverable; 5 is cosmetic. Finding 1 is the one real unintended-release path, low-probability on this single-maintainer, single-branch estate and recoverable (delete release + tag). On that basis the green apply PRs were merged as-is with each comment answered and linked here.

## Suggested flow

Fix the template in `src/apply.js` (+ tests), then true up the eight deployed copies — either via the existing policy-drift detection or a one-off apply pass — so all repos converge on the hardened version.

openIssues.title: maintainer-review-reply invents an ask when the caller says there is none
openIssues.body:
`maintainer-review-reply` has no branch for "there is no ask", so it manufactures one. On a clean approval it appended `Can you confirm you are happy for this to be merged?`, addressed to the contributor, when the maintainer is the person doing the merging.

The call, on `pr-agent` at `2026-08-31T06:27:01Z`:

```
--recipe maintainer-review-reply \
  --var verdict="Approving as-is, nothing to change" \
  --var ask="none, this is a clean approval" \
  --var recipient="apoorvdarshan"
```

Step 3 of the prompt template is unconditional: "What you are asking the contributor to do next, derived from the ask topic below and phrased as a direct question or request to the reader in the second person." There is no way to say there is nothing. `none, this is a clean approval` is read as a topic and rendered as a question, and the skeleton reinforces it by ending `<the ask, as a question>?`.

`{{ask}}` is also documented as required in the frontmatter `inputs` block, unlike `{{recipient}}` and `{{signoff}}` which are `string?`. So the recipe has no supported no-ask path at all, and a clean approval is a normal maintainer reply.

Two suggested changes, either would do:

1. Make `ask` optional (`ask: string?`) and add to the template: if no ask is given, stop after the evidence, and do not invent a next step for the contributor.
2. Add a guard alongside the existing anti-hallucination list: never ask the contributor to confirm, approve or authorise a merge. Merging is the maintainer's own action, so that question is never correct in this recipe's voice.

The second is worth having regardless of the first, because it is the specific fabrication that showed up rather than a generic one.

Recorded as a MISS against `2026-08-31T06:27:01Z` with the shipped final, which was two sentences and no ask.

openIssues.title: Boundary hook is blind to commands inside a wrapper script, which is what worktree isolation forces
openIssues.body:
## Summary

`scripts/delegate-boundary-hook.sh` classifies over the leading tokens of each shell segment, so a boundary command invoked through a wrapper script is invisible to it. The hook exits at the line 76 pre-filter and writes no row at all: no nag, and nothing in the trigger-rate denominator. This is distinct from #358, which is about the `Write` that authors a body file and about `--body-file` posts landing as `pre-drafted`. Here there is no row of any kind.

## Verified

Both forms run against the same payload on 2026-08-28, with `DELEGATE_LOCAL_NO_METRICS=1` so the metrics file was not touched:

```
$ echo '{"tool_input":{"command":"git commit -F /tmp/msg4.txt"},"cwd":"<repo>"}' | bash delegate-boundary-hook.sh
{"hookSpecificOutput":{...,"additionalContext":"delegate-local: about to author a git-commit message inline ..."}}

$ echo '{"tool_input":{"command":"bash /tmp/do-commit.sh"},"cwd":"<repo>"}' | bash delegate-boundary-hook.sh
(no output, exit 0)
```

## Why this is not a niche path

Claude Code's worktree-isolation guard refuses compound or substitution-bearing commands in a worktree-isolated session ("this command is too complex to verify that it stays inside the worktree"). The documented workaround, already recorded in my own notes for this skill, is to put the call in a small wrapper script and run that. It refused a `delegate.sh` invocation twice during this very session, and the wrapper was the only way through.

So the sessions most likely to route commands through a wrapper are worktree-isolated ones, which are exactly the long autonomous batches where delegation compliance matters most. The sensor goes quiet precisely where it is most needed.

## Circumstantial, and flagged as such

On 2026-08-27 in project `ismaelmartinez.me.uk` the hook logged 24 opportunity rows, the last at 13:02, against 4 delegations. Two commits followed at 13:38 and 14:01 and produced no opportunity row of either kind. The wrapper mechanism above is the probable cause, but I did not capture the exact command line at the time, so treat the attribution as probable rather than proven. The mechanism itself is proven independently by the test above.

## Suggested direction, not a prescription

Detecting a boundary command inside an arbitrary script is not generally solvable, and chasing it would be worse than the gap. Two cheaper options seem worth weighing:

- If the command's leading token is an interpreter (`bash`, `sh`, `zsh`) invoked on a path inside a known scratch or job directory, read that file and classify its contents. Narrow, and it covers the worktree-guard workaround specifically.
- Or record a distinct `state:"opaque"` row when the pre-filter fails but the raw string matched the cheap grep, so wrapper-hidden boundaries are visible as a known blind spot in the metric rather than silently absent from it.

## Verifiable goal

A `git commit -m` inside a wrapper script produces a row, of whatever state is decided, rather than nothing.

openIssues.title: Release PR workflow runs are held for approval, so the required check never reports
openIssues.body:
Release-please PRs do not clear the `repo-butler/copilot-code-review` gate, so every release needs an admin override. 0.28.0 shipped that way on 2026-08-26.

- `#409` sat `BLOCKED` with `mergeable: MERGEABLE`, no required status checks, no bypass actors on the only ruleset, one Copilot review in state `COMMENTED` on the current head sha `70477019`, and `reviewThreads.totalCount` of 0. Ordinary PRs with that exact shape (`#432`, `#433`) merge first time.
- The one structural difference is that `#409` is authored by `github-actions[bot]` and its review was requested by hand via `POST /pulls/409/requested_reviewers` rather than fired by `review_on_push`. Unverified hypothesis: the rule tracks its own automatic run, not the presence of a review.
- Separately and now verified, the gate also blocks on any unresolved Copilot thread even when GitHub marks it `isOutdated`. `#434` was `BLOCKED` with two such threads and went `CLEAN` the moment `resolveReviewThread` ran on both. Replying does not resolve, which is the trap.

Next release is the measurement: check whether the gate clears on its own before reaching for `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`.

openIssues.title: Before v1: revoke the agent's unattended gh pr merge permission
openIssues.body:
`.claude/settings.local.json` grants `Bash(gh pr merge:*)` so the agent can merge without a prompt per PR. That was added deliberately on 2026-08-18 to unblock a long autonomous backlog run, and it is appropriate for a solo-maintainer tool in early development. It is not appropriate once this has users.

Before tagging v1.0.0, remove the rule:

```json
"allow": [
  "Bash(gh pr merge --admin *)",
  "Bash(gh pr merge:*)"     <-- delete this line
]
```

The narrower `Bash(gh pr merge --admin *)` entry predates this and is a separate decision; it exists because release PRs cannot pass their required check (see #366) and so can only be merged with `--admin`. Fixing #366 removes the reason for that one too, at which point both can go and every merge returns to being an explicit human action.

Worth doing at the same time: re-read `CLAUDE.md`'s standing rule that a passing pipeline is not permission to merge. This grant is a deliberate, scoped exception to it, and v1 is the right moment for the exception to lapse.

openIssues.title: Install from the published skill instead of symlinking the dev checkout
openIssues.body:
## Summary

Both profiles symlink the skill at the live dev checkout, which is the wrong default because an agent session that leaves the checkout mid-rebase, on a feature branch, or with uncommitted edits silently changes skill behaviour for every other agent on both profiles, with no signal at the point of use.

## Evidence

Both Claude Code profiles symlink the skill directly at the working git checkout:

```
~/.claude-home/skills/delegate-local -> ~/projects/github/delegate-local
~/.claude-work/skills/delegate-local -> ~/projects/github/delegate-local
```

`~/.claude` is itself a symlink to `~/.claude-home`. So there is exactly one copy of the skill on the machine, it is a git working tree, and every agent on both profiles executes whatever commit that tree happens to be checked out at. That checkout currently also hosts six git worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/`, on branches `feat/mlx-reasoning-preference`, `docs/phase-18-expansion-research`, `docs/expansion-use-cases`, `docs/contributor-readiness`, `fix/dashboard-bargauge-instant` and `docs/cheap-first-economics`.

On 2026-08-16 the boundary hook was reported as "it fires but nothing happens" for other agents on the machine. One of the two root causes was that the checkout sat several commits behind `main`, so none of the merged hook fixes were live for any agent. The fix required a manual `git pull` in the checkout. The other cause was a bug in the nudge, fixed in PR #359 (`11864f3`).

## Proposed change

`README.md` documents `npx skills add IsmaelMartinez/delegate-local -a claude-code -g`. The `skills` CLI (verified via `npx skills@latest --help`) supports `update [skills...]`, `list`, `remove`, and an `experimental_install` that restores from a `skills-lock.json`. It symlinks into agent directories by default from a shared store, or copies with `--copy`. The one skill on this machine installed that way, `yes-flag-test-skill`, resolves as `~/.claude/skills/yes-flag-test-skill -> ../../.agents/skills/yes-flag-test-skill`, so the shared store is `~/.agents/skills/`. That gives a pinned, updatable version decoupled from the dev checkout, which is the property missing today.

## Constraints to handle

First, the work profile lives at `~/.claude-work`, which is not a path the `skills` CLI knows. `-a claude-code -g` resolves to `~/.claude/skills`, i.e. the home profile only. The work profile needs either a second install with the config dir pointed at it, or a hand-made symlink from `~/.claude-work/skills/delegate-local` to the shared `~/.agents/skills/delegate-local`.

Second, metrics and per-user config currently land inside the repo. The default metrics path in `scripts/delegate.sh:382` is `${DELEGATE_METRICS_FILE:-$HOME/.claude/skills/delegate-local/metrics.jsonl}`, which today resolves through the symlink to the repo root. The file is 1.1 MB and 4628 rows of accumulated history, spanning 2026-05-03 to 2026-08-16. `.gitignore` already documents and ignores this ("The default metrics path ... resolves through the `npx skills add`-installed symlink back to the repo root for anyone developing the skill while it's installed"), and does the same for `/config.sh` and `/profile.sh` written by `scripts/onboard.sh`. After the migration those paths resolve into `~/.agents/skills/delegate-local` instead, which `skills update` may replace. The existing history has to be moved deliberately and `DELEGATE_METRICS_FILE` pointed somewhere stable and outside any managed skill directory, or the calibration history is lost on the first update.

## Development story afterwards

The dev checkout stops being the thing that runs. Testing an unmerged change means either running scripts from the checkout by path, or temporarily repointing one profile's symlink. That trade is the point of the change, but it should be written down in the repo so the next session does not "fix" it by symlinking back.

openIssues.title: Boundary hook never observes the drafting moment for write-then-post bodies
openIssues.body:
## Summary
Issue #349 identified two halves of the same problem and PR #355 shipped only the first. This issue tracks the second.

## What PR #355 shipped
PR #355 shipped the cheap option #349 proposed. A `gh`/`glab` post whose body comes from a file that already exists (`--body-file`, `--notes-file`, `--file`, `-F`, including `gh api -F body=@draft.md`) is now recorded with `state:"pre-drafted"` and does not nudge. Pre-drafted rows sit outside the trigger-rate ratio entirely — neither numerator nor denominator — so human-approved posts no longer deflate the per-project rate that issue #277 is measuring. This is documented in `docs/boundary-hook.md`.

## What remains
The drafting moment itself is never observed. `scripts/delegate-boundary-hook.sh` runs as a `PreToolUse` hook on the `Bash` tool only, so the earlier `Write` that authors the body file passes unseen. The result is that the write-then-post path is now correctly excluded from the metric but is still not captured as an opportunity — the sensor has gone quiet rather than becoming accurate. A body file drafted inline by the agent and a body file drafted on-device via a recipe are indistinguishable to the hook, and both are recorded as `pre-drafted`.

## Possible direction
A second `PreToolUse` hook on the `Write` tool that fires when the target path looks like a post body (a scratch draft destined for `--body-file`) and records the opportunity at the moment the text is actually authored is under consideration. No decision has been made. Open questions include how to identify such a path without a large false-positive rate on ordinary file writes, whether the two hooks would double-count when a write-then-post pair both fire, and whether the `Write` payload carries enough to tell an agent-authored draft from one the human dictated.

## Out of scope
The human-review half stays out of scope. Issue #349 already judged it as "probably has no clean signal in the payload", and nothing in PR #355 changed that.

## [2.11.0](https://github.com/IsmaelMartinez/teams-for-linux/compare/v2.10.0...v2.11.0) (2026-05-27)

**NOTE: Superseded by https://github.com/IsmaelMartinez/teams-for-linux/releases/tag/v2.11.1 a build failure meant 2.11.0 didn't get any artifacts.**

teams-for-linux 2.11.0 is out with new sticker support and improved Home Assistant integration.

## Highlights
- Custom stickers MVP: add your own stickers to the chat panel (#2550). opt-in
- MQTT + Home Assistant: new microphone (#2497), camera (#2582) and incoming-call (#2572) topics, with Home Assistant auto-discovery so entities are created for you
- Wayland screen sharing fixed: getDisplayMedia now routes through the in-app picker (#2534). Please report if you got any issues after the upgrade.
- WM_CLASS / --class fix: custom window class reaches both X11 and Wayland again, fixing the v2.10.0 regression (#2569)
- Diagnostics cleanup: quieter pre-login logs, full PII sanitising of renderer logs, and a crisper macOS dock icon (#2560). We get a lot of noise in the logs from Microsoft side.
- Electron bumped to 41.7.1 (#2583)

## [2.10.0](https://github.com/IsmaelMartinez/teams-for-linux/compare/v2.9.0...v2.10.0) (2026-05-19)

2.10.0 lands **FIDO2 hardware security keys**, the **multi-account Manage dialog**, and a redesigned **full-window screen-share picker**, alongside fixes for MCAS auth, SharePoint concurrent downloads, and the ozone x11 default. Most new features are opt-in via config; only the screen-share picker is on by default.

### How to enable each new feature

Add the relevant block to your `config.json`:

```json
{
  "auth": { "webauthn": { "enabled": true } },
  "multiAccount": { "enabled": true },
  "download": { "enabled": true },
  "notifications": { "timeoutType": "never" }
}
```

- **`auth.webauthn.enabled`** — FIDO2 hardware security keys. Linux only, requires the `fido2-tools` system package (`apt install fido2-tools` / `dnf install fido2-tools` / `pacman -S libfido2`). Silent no-op on macOS and Windows.
- **`multiAccount.enabled`** — multi-account profile manager (Add / Switch / rename / remove). Mutually exclusive with `auth.intune.enabled`; if both are true, multi-account is auto-disabled with a startup warning.
- **`download.enabled`** — master switch for download completion toast and taskbar progress. Once on, sub-flags `notifyOnDownloadComplete`, `showProgressBar`, and `showTitlePrefix` each default `true` and can be turned off individually.
- **`notifications.timeoutType: "never"`** — persistent notifications on Linux and Windows (workaround for GNOME and other desktops that auto-clear). Choices are `default` or `never`.

Always-on this release (no config needed): the new screen-share picker overlay, the SharePoint QUIC fix, the MCAS proxy cookie-domain fix, telemetry beacon blocking, and log-noise cleanup.

> **Multi-account is a work-in-progress preview.** The new `multiAccount.enabled` flag (off by default) lets you keep separate Teams sessions in the same window. openIssues.title: Evaluate upgrading to Electron 43

labels.name: dependencies
labels.description: Pull requests that update a dependency file

openIssues.body:
## Why now

Electron 42 reaches end of life on 2026-10-20, about seven weeks out. Electron 43 went stable on 2026-06-30 and is already on 43.5.0, so the series is mature enough to move onto.

## Why not 44

Electron 44 removed all 32-bit builds, Windows ia32 and Linux armv7l. There is no `electron-v44.0.0-linux-armv7l.zip`, so the download 404s and both armv7l jobs fail. That is what killed #2926, and it is not something we can patch around.

Electron 43 is the last series shipping prebuilt 32-bit ARM, and 43.5.0 still carries all seven armv7l assets. It reaches end of life on 2027-01-05, so whether we keep publishing an armv7l package is a decision that arrives by January whichever version we run. Worth taking deliberately rather than letting a dependabot PR make it for us.

## What to check before bumping

Two breaking changes in 43 plausibly touch us, both cosmetic:

- Frameless windows on Linux now get rounded corners. We have four (incoming call toast, login, notification toast, quick chat), plus the main window for anyone running `frame: false`. Opt out per window with `roundedCorners: false` if it looks wrong.
- File dialogs default to Downloads when no `defaultPath` is passed, which changes the app icon picker in `app/menus/index.js`.

Everything else in the 43 breaking-change list greps clean against our code. electron-builder stays pinned at 26.15.7: it already built Electron 44 for every 64-bit target on #2926, so it is not the constraint here.

## What we get

Wayland fixes worth having: desktopCapturer thumbnail generation, and a premature portal timeout.

Nothing in 43 or 44 unblocks #2714. The only upstream WebAuthn work is macOS Touch ID, and that was already backported into 42.

Two Linux fixes land in 44 rather than 43, and are the reason to move again afterwards: tray icons on desktops that address StatusNotifierItem by unique D-Bus name, and `setBadgeCount` / `setProgressBar` restored on Linux without libunity.

## Target

A matured 43.x rather than 43.0.0, matching how we went from 41.7.1 straight to 42.3.0.

openIssues.title: [Bug]: signing in asks for one security key touch per registered credential

labels.name: release ready
labels.description: Fix merged to main, included in the next release

openIssues.body:
Signing in with a hardware key against an account with several registered credentials asked for one touch per listed credential. `getAssertion` ran a full `fido2-assert` per entry, so the key blinked, the user touched, the key answered "no such credential" for an entry belonging to another authenticator, and the next attempt wanted another touch. Five touches to sign in, with nothing indicating more than one was expected.

Fixed in #2889 by probing each allowed credential with a silent assertion (`fido2-assert -t up=false`) before involving the user, then running the real assertion against the single credential that matched. Falls back to the old sequential loop when nothing probes as present.

Found and fixed by @nikolainyegaard, hardware-verified by @marcovr.

openIssues.title: [Bug]: unhandled EPIPE when the FIDO2 PIN is written to an exited child closes the app

labels.name: release ready
labels.description: Fix merged to main, included in the next release

openIssues.body:
## Problem

`spawnFido2` in `app/webauthn/fido2Backend.js` writes to the child's stdin twice: the credential parameters right after spawn, and the PIN from inside the stderr handler once a chunk containing `Enter PIN for` arrives.

```js
// app/webauthn/fido2Backend.js:118-123
if (!pinWritten && pin && chunk.includes("Enter PIN for")) {
  pinWritten = true;
  log.info("[WEBAUTHN] PIN prompt detected, writing PIN");
  proc.stdin.write(pin.trim() + "\n");
  proc.stdin.end();
}
```

There is no `error` listener on `proc.stdin` anywhere in the module. When the child's stdin read end is already closed, either write raises `EPIPE` as an unhandled exception rather than an error on the stream.

`app/index.js:55` then routes every `uncaughtException` through `isNetworkError`, whose pattern list (`app/config/defaults.js:9`) is entirely Chromium `ERR_*` strings. `write EPIPE` matches none of them, so it falls through to `process.exit(1)` and the whole app closes.

## Reproduction

Deterministic against the real `spawnFido2` with a stub binary that closes fd 0 before printing the prompt:

```
[closeSync(0)-then-linger]              !! UNCAUGHT EPIPE: write EPIPE
[child merely exits after prompting]    no EPIPE
```

So it is a race rather than a guaranteed failure on every run, and the robust trigger is a child that closes its read end before we write. A cancel can also reach it, but only inside the window before Node tears the stdio streams down: killing the process group and writing about 150ms later gives `ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED` delivered to the write callback, with no uncaught exception.

## Impact

Any fido2 spawn, so both credential creation and assertion. The feature is opt-in beta behind the WebAuthn flag, so this only reaches people who have turned it on. #2917 adds a second PIN-carrying spawn per discoverable sign-in and so widens the window, though it did not introduce this.

## Proposed fix

Attach an `error` listener to `proc.stdin`, registered before either write, so a dead pipe cannot become an uncaught exception. It should log at `warn` rather than `debug`: `log.debug` is off unless `auth.webauthn.debug` is set, and the case most worth seeing is a failed *parameter* write, where the tool never receives its input and the only other symptom is the full timeout a minute later.

Guarding the PIN write on the not-rejected, not-exited state was also tried and then dropped. The listener alone fixes the crash, no test detects such a guard's absence, and in this failure the child closes stdin without exiting, so `exited` is false and it would never have fired.

openIssues.title: [Feat]: write a migrated nested copy of config.json so users can adopt the ADR-025 names in one step

labels.name: release ready
labels.description: Fix merged to main, included in the next release

openIssues.body:
Follow-up to #2842. The ADR-025 rename table is landing in batches, and the flat names keep working until 2.30.0. Deprecation notices are log-only as of the batch 2 branch, so nobody is interrupted today, but when the removal approaches people will need to actually move their config and there is no tooling to help them do it.

## Why a file, not a copy/paste block

The obvious shape is "here is your config rewritten with the new names, paste it over the old one". The problem is that a pasteable block on screen trains people to paste their config into issue threads when asking for help, and a config file carries MQTT broker URLs and credentials, custom background service URLs, proxy servers and client certificate paths.

Writing the result to a file beside `config.json` avoids that. The startup log names only the path, never a value, so the invariant that `app/config/deprecation.js` and `app/config/validator.js` both hold is preserved. The user reviews the file and moves it over when they are ready, so nothing is rewritten under them and a bad transform cannot break a working install.

## Why this is cheaper than ADR-025 implies

ADR-025 lists as a negative consequence that "the four inversions mean a naive key-copy migration would silently flip user intent, so tooling must consult the Inverted column. This table is hand-maintained and can drift from `app/config/options.js`". Both halves are already handled in code. `app/config/renames.js` carries `flat`, `nested`, `inverted` and `type` per entry, and `tests/unit/configRenames.test.js` pins the table against `options.js` so it cannot drift silently.

`getConfigFile` in `app/config/index.js` is `require()` on the `.json` path, so the file is plain JSON with no comment support. A rewrite destroys nothing but key ordering and whitespace, which removes the usual objection to automated config migration.

The transform itself is close to an inversion of `applyRenamedOptions`: walk `RENAMES`, project the flat key onto the nested path instead of the other way round, negating where `inverted` is set.

## Inversions are all in batch 3

Worth recording because it affects sequencing. None of the 38 renames on the batch 2 branch set `inverted`. All four inversions (`disableNotifications`, `disableNotificationSound`, `disableNotificationWindowFlash`, `disableBadgeCount`) target `notifications.*`, which is one of the four already-shipped namespaces held behind gate A. So for everything landing now a migration is a pure key rename, and `coerce()` already negates polarity by the time the risky cases arrive.

## Proposal

A pure transform in `app/config/renames.js` producing a nested copy of the user's config file, plus a Settings menu entry that writes it on demand. Regenerating on demand rather than writing at startup keeps it from going stale against a config edited afterwards, and keeps it out of the startup path entirely.

The menu entry belongs beside the "Open config file" and "Open config folder" entries from #2885, so it depends on #2893 landing first. The transform does not, and can go in on its own.

## Sequencing

Log-only now, which is on the batch 2 branch and removes the pressure. The helper built before 2.30.0 approaches. The startup modal restored at that point, pointing at the helper, so the one time people are interrupted is the one time there is something to do and a one-click way to do it.

openIssues.title: [Bug]: Clicking a notification focuses the window but does not open the sending chat

labels.name: release ready
labels.description: Fix merged to main, included in the next release

openIssues.body:
Split out of #2768, where @sedax90 confirmed the notification *content* is now correct but reported that clicking the notification brings Teams to the front on the previously open chat rather than the one that sent the message.

### What happens

Clicking a notification focuses the window and stops there. The conversation that raised the notification is never opened.

### Why

On `notificationMethod` `electron` and `custom`, `app/browser/preload.js` builds the notification in the main process and hands Teams a stub object back. Teams attaches its own click handler to that stub, and that handler is the part that knows which conversation the message came from.

`app/notifications/service.js` handles the click by calling `show()` or `restoreWindow()` on the main window and nothing else. The click is never relayed to the renderer, so Teams' handler never runs. `app/notificationSystem/index.js` `#handleToastClick` does the same for the custom toast.

The `web` default is unaffected: it returns the real `Notification` object, so Teams' handler is wired directly and fires normally.

This is less an oversight than an un-revisited scope decision. [ADR-022](https://ismaelmartinez.github.io/teams-for-linux/development/adr/022-custom-notification-toast-scope) records focus-only as deliberate for the custom toast's Phase 1, and #2647 added `notifications.electron.clickAction` (`show` / `restore` / `none`), which is entirely about window behaviour and never considered passing the click onward.

### The fix

Relay the click to the renderer keyed by the `notificationId` we already generate, reusing the mechanism `notification-closed` uses today, and invoke the stub's handler. We do not need to know which chat the notification came from; Teams' own callback does.

Verified locally with an Electron probe: relaying by id fires a handler set either via `onclick =` or `addEventListener('click')`, and a mismatched id is ignored.

### Still unverified

Whether Teams' handler navigates rather than merely focusing. That needs a signed-in account to confirm, which is what the linked PR is for.

openIssues.title: [Feat]: Add an "Open config file" menu entry

labels.name: awaiting user feedback
labels.description: Waiting for user to confirm they still need this feature

openIssues.body:
## Problem

There is no way to reach `config.json` from inside the app. `git grep` over `app/menus/` finds no `shell.openPath` or `showItemInFolder` anywhere, so a user who wants to change any of the 68 restart-only options has to know the file exists, know its name, and know where their packaging format puts it.

That last part is the real friction, because the location is different for every format:

| Install | Config directory |
| --- | --- |
| deb / rpm / tar.gz / AppImage | `~/.config/teams-for-linux` |
| snap | `~/snap/teams-for-linux/current/.config/teams-for-linux/` |
| flatpak (`--user`) | `~/.var/app/com.github.IsmaelMartinez.teams_for_linux/config/teams-for-linux` |
| from source | `~/.config/Electron/` |

The Flatpak and Snap paths in particular are not somewhere anyone guesses.

## Proposal

Two entries under the existing **Settings** submenu in `app/menus/appMenu.js` (`getSettingsMenu`), next to Save and Restore:

- **Open config file** — `shell.openPath(getConfigFilePath(configPath))`
- **Open config folder** — `shell.openPath(configPath)`

The directory is already available as `AppConfiguration.configPath` (`app/appConfiguration/index.js:43`), and `app/config/index.js` has `getConfigFilePath(configPath)` for the file itself. `app/menus/index.js` already destructures from `electron`, so this is adding `shell` to that import plus the two handlers.

## Worth deciding

**Settled:** `config.json` frequently does not exist. The startup log says `No config file found (user or system-wide), using default values`, and `shell.openPath` on a missing path just returns an error string rather than doing anything useful. So "Open config file" writes an empty `{}` stub first when the file is absent, then opens it. Creating the directory if needed is part of that.

Also worth checking before implementing: whether `shell.openPath` actually escapes the sandbox on Flatpak and Snap. It goes through the portal on Flatpak, which normally handles `~/.var/app/...` fine since the app owns that directory, but it is worth confirming on both rather than assuming.

## Context

Came out of #2830, which proposed a full in-app settings window and was closed. 68 of the 74 config options are `applyMode: restart` and the 6 `live` ones are already exposed as menu toggles, so a settings window was mostly a GUI for options that need a restart anyway. Discoverability was the part of that idea actually worth keeping, and this is the cheap version of it.

openIssues.title: [Chore]: automate the Flathub beta-branch version bump
openIssues.body:
Bumping the Flathub `beta` branch after a pre-release is manual today. #2833 records why: Flathub's external-data-checker only runs against a repo's default branch, which is `master`, so the `update-*` PRs it opens never cover `beta`. The packaging repo's own `1491b72c` says the same in one line, "docs: note that the beta bump is manual".

Doing it by hand for 2.17.0 (flathub/com.github.IsmaelMartinez.teams_for_linux#217) came to three `url` and `sha256` pairs in `com.github.IsmaelMartinez.teams_for_linux.yml`: the x86_64 deb, the aarch64 deb, and the metainfo XML at the release tag. That is mechanical enough to automate.

## Why it is easy from here

Most of the logic already exists in `.github/workflows/flatpak-smoke.yml`. It fires on `release: [published]`, resolves the tag, and already picks `beta` over `master` by reading `isPrerelease`. What it deliberately does not do is compute checksums, because it swaps the remote sources for local downloads instead.

The checksums are cheaper than expected. Both deb hashes come straight off the release asset `digest` field, no download required. I verified that field against a locally downloaded 113MB amd64 deb for 2.17.0 and it matched exactly. Only the metainfo needs fetching, and it is a few KB.

## Proposal

A sibling workflow on `release: [published]`, guarded on `isPrerelease`, that parses the published beta manifest, rewrites only the sources it actually references, and opens a PR against `beta`. Parse rather than assume: releases also carry an armv7l deb that the manifest does not reference, so a blind find-and-replace would drift.

Leave the merge manual, at least initially. Flathub's own `builds/x86_64` runs on PRs into `beta` and gates the merge, and publishing happens on merge, so an automated PR still gets a real build before anything reaches testers. Auto-merge on green is a later decision, not part of this.

## The one real cost

It needs a token. The packaging repo is under the `flathub` org and has no `.github/workflows` of its own, so the push has to come from here, which means a fine-grained PAT scoped to that single repo with contents and pull-requests write, stored as a secret. There is no such secret today. That is the trade to weigh: a stored credential against a five-minute manual edit per pre-release.

If that trade is not worth it, the cheaper half is still worth having: have the release workflow post the exact diff (the three url/sha256 pairs, already computed) as a comment or job summary, so the manual bump becomes copy and paste rather than re-deriving hashes each time.

Refs #2833

openIssues.title: [Bug]: Screen sharing fails on native Ubuntu Wayland

labels.name: awaiting user feedback
labels.description: Waiting for user to confirm they still need this feature

openIssues.body:
### Can you reproduce this bug on the Microsoft Teams web app (https://teams.microsoft.com)?

No

### Describe the bug

On native Ubuntu Wayland, starting screen sharing does not open a usable source-selection flow. The camera stops and Teams reports either:

- “Your video isn't working. We couldn't access your camera.”
- “There's an issue with content sharing. Something went wrong. Try again later.”

The problem appears to be caused by `--use-fake-ui-for-media-stream` preventing the PipeWire portal chooser from opening. Removing that flag allows selection, but the current custom picker then causes repeated portal selection and source-ID mismatches.

### What package are you using?

snap

### Version

2.15.0

### Reproduction steps

1. Run Teams for Linux in a native Ubuntu Wayland session.
2. Join a Teams call with the camera enabled.
3. Select Share.
4. Select “Screen, window, or tab.”
5. Observe that no usable source chooser appears.
6. After a few seconds, the camera stops and Teams displays a camera or content-sharing error.

### Expected Behavior

1. Selecting screen sharing should open the Ubuntu xdg-desktop-portal chooser.
2. The user should select a screen or window once.
3. Sharing should start immediately without disabling the camera.

### Debug

```bash
ELECTRON_ENABLE_LOGGING=true teams-for-linux --logConfig='{"transports":{"console":{"level":"debug"}}}'
```

Environment:

- Ubuntu 26.04 LTS
- GNOME
- `XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`
- Kernel 7.0.0-29-generic
- x86_64

The application starts with `WebRTCPipeWireCapturer` enabled, but also adds `--use-fake-ui-for-media-stream`. On native Wayland this suppresses the PipeWire portal selection flow.

Removing that switch allows the Ubuntu portal chooser to open. However, the custom picker calls `desktopCapturer.getSources()`, and re-enumerating sources creates another portal session with different transient source IDs. This produces repeated picker transitions or causes selection to fail.

Using one `desktopCapturer.getSources()` call and passing its returned source directly to the `setDisplayMediaRequestHandler` callback allows sharing to work.

### Additional context

The issue was reproduced with three displays on Ubuntu GNOME Wayland.

A working implementation requires:

- Do not add `--use-fake-ui-for-media-stream` on native Wayland.
- Keep it only for legacy XWayland where required.
- On native Wayland, call `desktopCapturer.getSources()` once to open `xdg-desktop-portal`.
- Pass the returned source directly to Teams.
- Do not open the custom picker or re-enumerate sources, because PipeWire source IDs are session-specific.

The Microsoft Teams web app does not exhibit the issue because the browser uses the native portal flow directly.

openIssues.title: [Feat]: Config migration: move the remaining 55 flat options to nested names (ADR-025)
openIssues.body:
Tracking issue for the remaining flat to nested configuration migration, following the convention and rename table settled in [ADR-025](https://github.com/IsmaelMartinez/teams-for-linux/blob/main/docs-site/docs/development/adr/025-config-option-naming-convention.md).

`app/config/options.js` declares 72 top level options today. 17 are already nested objects and 55 remain flat, and every one of those 55 has an agreed nested target in the ADR-025 rename table. Verified 2026-08-15 against `docs-site/static/config-schema.json`: none of the 55 have moved, and zero of their nested targets resolve. Four of the target namespaces (`notifications`, `idleDetection`, `auth`, `network`) already ship as objects holding unrelated leaves, so 18 of the 55 are leaf additions to an existing namespace and the other 37 need 12 brand new namespaces.

## Approach

Additive duplication rather than migration. For each namespace we declare the nested keys, mark the flat ones `deprecated`, and let **both** keep working for a long window. Internal read sites keep reading the flat names; the loader back-fills them from the nested names after parsing, so no feature code is swept during the window. The flat declarations and the back-fill layer are deleted together at the end.

Precedence uses `yargsInstance.parsed.defaulted`, which lists exactly the keys that fell back to their declared default. The nested value only wins when the nested key is absent from `defaulted`, meaning the user actually supplied it. Four renames invert a boolean and must be negated on projection.

Removal target is **2.30.0**. At the 2026 median of roughly 13 days between minor releases that is about six months from 2.17.0, which is the window for people who skip releases. Note the count is in minors: 47 of the last 60 releases were patches, so "ten to twenty releases" measured in tags would only be one to two months.

## Iterations

Ordered least disruptive first. "Threads" is the number of distinct issue or PR threads mentioning the option, measured 2026-08-15 across 2,708 issues and 15,447 comments, used as a proxy for how many users actually set it.

| Batch | Namespaces | Opts | Threads | Notes | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | infrastructure | 0 | | aggregated deprecation warning (#2858) | done, ships 2.17.0 |
| 1 | `shortcuts`, `storage` | 3 | 13, 15 | new namespaces, no machinery, near invisible | merged [#2859](https://github.com/IsmaelMartinez/teams-for-linux/pull/2859), ships 2.17.0 |
| 2 | `customBackground`, `urlHandling`, `incomingCalls` | 9 | 23, 34, 36 | new namespaces, self contained | |
| 3 | `network`, `auth` | 7 | 19, 39 | first existing-namespace renames; needs gate A | |
| 4 | `appearance`, `idleDetection`, `platform` | 11 | 67, 42, 84 | renderer reads via `get-config` start here | |
| 5 | `app`, `window`, `tray` | 14 | 135, 138, 147 | high reach; `class` is consumed pre-window | |
| 6 | `notifications`, `performance`, `development` | 11 | 115, 123, 229 | needs gate B; hardest mechanics | |

Per-namespace option lists are in the ADR-025 rename table.

## Gates

**Gate A, before batch 3.** Note since #2859: the projection decides presence from the raw config file, not from the resolved config, so it is already safe against this change. Reading the resolved config would have meant every unset leaf resolved to its default the day deep merging landed, overwriting what the user set. yargs replaces object options wholesale instead of deep merging them, verified against yargs 18.1.0: with a default of `{enabled:true, sound:{enabled:true}}`, a config file containing only `notifications:{sound:{enabled:false}}` resolves to `{"sound":{"enabled":false}}` and `enabled` disappears. This is pre-existing and does not affect batches 1 and 2, because nothing reads those new namespaces directly during the window. It does affect every namespace that already ships leaves, so it must be fixed before `network`, `auth`, `idleDetection` and `notifications`.

**Gate B, before batch 6.** Deprecation warnings only inspect the config file (`app/config/deprecation.js`), so an option passed as a CLI flag or environment variable produces no warning at all. This matters most for exactly the batch 6 options: `webDebug` accounts for 223 of that batch's threads and is almost entirely `--webDebug`, the standard debugging instruction, and `disableGpu` and `electronCLIFlags` are troubleshooting-doc flags. Without this, those users would be silently ignored at removal having never seen a warning.

## Why `notifications` is last

It is the only namespace with inverted booleans (four of them), the only one with `applyMode: live`, four of its options are read in the renderer, and its six menu-toggle keys are persisted in `legacyConfigStore` and re-applied by `loadMenuToggleSettings()` in `app/index.js` *after* config resolution, which would clobber any precedence logic. Every hard mechanic in the migration is concentrated there.

## Incidental findings

- `spellCheckerLanguages` is written to `legacyConfigStore` at `app/mainAppWindow/index.js:840` but never read back, so that persistence is orphaned. Worth clearing up with batch 4.
- ADR-025 still describes #2841 as undecided and says the decision "must be settled before the first rename". That paragraph needs updating now the decision is made.
- No option has any functional packaging or external dependency; every hit in the appdata XML was historical release-note prose.

Prerequisite #2841 is settled. Refs #2597. Convention and full rename table in ADR-025.

labels.name: awaiting user feedback

openIssues.body:
### Can you reproduce this bug on the Microsoft Teams web app (https://teams.microsoft.com)?

Yes

### Describe the bug

In-app call/meeting audio is completely silent. Mic works (others hear me), but no incoming audio reaches any output device. The identical Microsoft web app (teams.cloud.microsoft) in a browser plays call audio correctly on the same machines, isolating the fault to the bundled Electron/Chromium render path. Reproduces on two independent CachyOS/Wayland machines (desktop: Intel+NVIDIA hybrid GPU; laptop: separate hardware).

### What package are you using?

aur

### Version

2.13.0 (also 2.10.0, 2.11.1) — Electron 42

### Reproduction steps

```markdown
1. Launch teams-for-linux on CachyOS (Wayland), sign in.
2. Make a test call (Settings → Devices → Make a test call / Echo).
3. Speak — the far end hears me fine (mic works).
4. No incoming/echo audio is heard from any output (speakers or Bluetooth headset).
5. Confirmed NOT device/routing: `pw-play` to the same sink plays fine, and all other apps play audio normally.
6. In-call WebRTC stats show packets received and OPUS-decoded, but PipeWire playback meters stay flat — audio is decoded but never rendered to the sink.
7. Opening teams.cloud.microsoft in a browser and making the same test call plays audio correctly, on both machines.
8. Persists across versions 2.10.0 / 2.11.1 / 2.13.0 (Electron 41/42).
```

### Expected Behavior

```markdown
Incoming call/meeting audio should play through the selected output device, the same way it does in the Microsoft Teams web app on the same machine.
```

### Debug

```markdown
ELECTRON_ENABLE_LOGGING=true teams-for-linux --logConfig='{"transports":{"console":{"level":"debug"}}}'
```

### Additional context

Audio is decoded but never rendered: in-call WebRTC stats show packets received and OPUS-decoded, while PipeWire playback meters stay flat. `pw-play` to the same sink plays fine and all other apps have working audio, ruling out device/routing. Reproduces on two independent CachyOS/Wayland machines; web app works on both.

openIssues.title: [Feat]: Passkey bridging to work around missing Passkey support
openIssues.body:
### Describe the feature

As discussed in #2714, there should be a way to configure a custom plugin / wrapper script / etc. for Passkey handling.

### Motivation

Right now, there is no unified Passkey solution on Linux like there is on Windows with Windows Hello and on MacOS with iCloud Keychain. 

Teams-for-Linux supports physical FIDO2 keys through the fido2-tools application, but it does not support Passkeys stored in 3rd-party password managers like KeepassXC, Bitwarden or 1Password. 

The fido2-tools only require the client data hash, but most other systems / password managers require the full client data JSON which is currently not provided by Teams-for-Linux. 

I would like to have a feature in Teams-for-Linux that'd allow people to write their own wrapper scripts to make Teams-for-Linux interface with their particular password manager for Passkey support, until [Passkey support on Linux](https://github.com/linux-credentials) has matured enough to be natively integrated.

That would mean that the path to the binary / binaries should be configurable in the config file instead of hardcoded to the fido2-tools, and there should be a way for Teams-for-Linux to pass the entire clientDataJSON to this application, not just the clientDataHash.

### Alternatives

- Using a physical passkey, but then I'd have to have a separate key just for Teams ...
- Waiting for https://github.com/linux-credentials, but I assume it'll still take quite a long time for this solution to be integrated into Linux distributions, and with Microsoft starting to push Passkeys more and more, I'd like to have a faster solution.

### Additional context

See previous conversation at #2714.

openIssues.title: [Bug]: Screen share picker selection always fails on Wayland/PipeWire — source IDs change between getSources() calls

labels.name: awaiting user feedback
labels.description: Waiting for user to confirm they still need this feature

openIssues.body:
### Can you reproduce this bug on the Microsoft Teams web app?

No

### Describe the bug

On Wayland with PipeWire, picking a source in the in-app screen share picker never works. The app logs `[SCREEN_SHARE] Selected source not found` and Teams shows a "can't access your camera" error. The cause is an ID mismatch in `findSelectedSource` — details below.

### What package are you using?

aur

### Version

2.11.1

### Reproduction steps

1. Wayland session (sway 1.12 / wlroots in my case, with xdg-desktop-portal-wlr 0.8.2 and PipeWire 1.6.7).
2. Default launch (`--ozone-platform=x11`), with `"wayland": { "xwaylandOptimizations": true }` in config.json so the portal request actually goes out (without it I hit the "selector never pops up" problem from #2707 — commented there separately).
3. Join a call, share screen, pick any source in the picker.
4. Sharing never starts. Teams complains about camera access.

### Expected Behavior

The source I picked gets shared.

### Debug

App log (debug level):

```
08:57:06.321 › [SCREEN_SHARE] Selected source not found
```

`xdg-desktop-portal-wlr -l DEBUG` shows the portal side is fine — a cast session opens, the PipeWire stream reaches "streaming", then the client closes it right away:

```
[INFO] - pipewire: stream state changed to "streaming"
[INFO] - pipewire: node id is 112
[INFO] - dbus: session closed
[DEBUG] - xdpw: destroying cast instance
```

I read this against the source and I think the bug is here:

```js
// app/mainAppWindow/index.js
function findSelectedSource(sources, source) {
  return sources.find((s) => s.id === source.id);
}
```

`handleScreenSourceSelection` calls `desktopCapturer.getSources()` a *second* time after the user already picked a source in the StreamSelector, then matches by exact ID. On PipeWire, every `getSources()` call opens a fresh portal session and the source IDs embed that session's PipeWire node ID — so the second call returns different IDs than the ones the picker showed. The match always fails, `callback({})` rejects the request, and Teams surfaces it as a camera error.

### Additional context

Possible fix: the StreamSelector already holds the full `DesktopCapturerSource` object, so on Wayland/PipeWire it could go straight to `callback({ video: source })` without re-querying. Matching by `name` as a fallback would also do it.

Workaround that works for me: launch with `--ozone-platform=wayland`. Then `getDisplayMedia` goes straight to the portal (in-app picker bypassed, as the comment in `injectedScreenSharing.js` describes) and sharing works reliably.

Related: #2707 (the "selector doesn't pop up" half of the story), #2534, #2217.

openIssues.title: [Feat]: Multi-account profile switcher (ADR-020 tracking)
openIssues.body:
## Summary

Tracking issue for the multi-account profile switcher work led by @jpenberthy, designed in [ADR-020](https://ismaelmartinez.github.io/teams-for-linux/development/adr/020-multi-account-profile-switcher/). Several PRs have already shipped to main and will land in 2.9.0; the rest of Phase 1 plus Phases 2 and 3 are ahead. This single issue is where to follow progress and coordinate; please do not refile separate tickets for the same feature, comment here instead.

The design is settled in ADR-020, this issue only tracks delivery.

## Status

### Phase 1: MVP

Per-profile `WebContentsView`s, top-right switcher overlay, `Profiles` menu with Add / Switch / Manage flows, `Ctrl+Alt+1…5` shortcuts, first-run Profile 0 migration, the six Phase 1 `profile-*` IPC channels, plus the audit-table shared-state migrations.

- [x] ADR-020 published (#2426)
- [x] `multiAccount.enabled` flag and Intune mutual-exclusion check (#2450)
- [x] `ProfilesManager` scaffold and login state migration (#2478)
- [x] Per-profile `WebContentsView` lifecycle + Profile 0 bootstrap (#2483)
- [x] `Profiles` submenu with Switch-to (#2489)
- [x] Add-profile dialog with first-run bootstrap fix (#2496)
- [x] Manage-profiles dialog (#2510)
- [x] Switcher chrome overlay (#2661, merged 2026-07-24; landed as a bottom-left pill, ADR erratum included)
- [x] Pin toggle (max 5) + `Ctrl+Alt+1…5` shortcuts for pinned profiles (#2787, merged 2026-08-10). Chord moved off the ADR's original `Ctrl+Shift`, which Teams web binds for its own app-bar nav. Two follow-ups split out to #2821
- [x] Screen-preview partition derived from active profile (audit row 2) — retired as not needed; preview no longer carries a session (#2534), confirmed in #2626 (2026-06-07)
- [x] `CustomBackground` per-instance refactor (audit row 3) — Phase 1 shared-state field move done in #2626 (2026-06-07); per-profile instantiation deferred to the per-view work
- [x] Byte-identity-when-disabled E2E smoke test (covered by `multi-account-disabled.spec.js`)

#### Phase 1 polish discovered post-MVP

- [x] Screen-share picker handler not bound to profile partition sessions (#2529)
- [ ] Meeting join and `msteams://` deep link route to Profile 0 rather than the active profile (#2867). ADR-020 Phase 1c.1 deliberately left both handlers, and auth recovery, on the root window; `ProfileViewManager` needs an accessor for the active view before any of them can be rerouted.

### Phase 2: Background notifications

Per-partition preload notification shim and unread-count tagging, aggregated tray badge, per-profile unread dots, `disableNotifications` and `muted` plumbing per profile.

- [x] Sender to profile attribution map, the foundation the rest of Phase 2 resolves through (#2865, merged 2026-08-28). Carried a user-facing fix too: removing a profile whose view had already closed itself skipped the partition storage clear, so the next tenant of that partition inherited the old data
- [ ] Descendant attribution (popups and `<webview>` guests) plus a profile-view window-open policy (#2916, in review, rebasing onto main now #2865 has landed)
- [ ] Per-partition preload notification shim
- [ ] Unread-count tagging
- [ ] Aggregated tray badge
- [ ] Per-profile unread dots
- [ ] `disableNotifications` and `muted` plumbing per profile

### Phase 3: Power features

`--profile-id` CLI flag end-to-end, keyboard shortcut to cycle profiles, pinned-profile sidebar (max 5), drag-to-reorder.

- [ ] `--profile-id` CLI flag end-to-end
- [ ] Keyboard shortcut to cycle profiles
- [ ] Pinned-profile sidebar (max 5)
- [ ] Drag-to-reorder

## Where to test

Set `"multiAccount": { "enabled": true }` in your config to opt in. With #2496 merged, the **Profiles → Add profile…** menu entry is wired up end-to-end, so you can add and switch between profiles from the UI. The Manage dialog (#2510) and the switcher pill (#2661) have both landed. Pinning and the `Ctrl+Alt+1…5` shortcuts are in review in #2787.

## Context

Originally requested in #72, #1656, #1830, #438, and tangentially via #1984 (which was redirected to ADR-010's Quick Chat as the alternative for that specific framing). Those tickets stay closed; subscribers will be redirected here for ongoing progress.

@jpenberthy this is the place to drop status updates, ETAs, and any "stuck on X" notes so the community can follow along and offer to take individual pieces. Thanks again for driving this.

releases.name: v1.0.0
releases.body:
WiFi Sentinel v1.0.0 — multi-persona WiFi and network security analyser.

Features:
- CLI scanner with 10 scanner modules and three-tier tool fallback
- Five AI-style persona agents (red team, blue team, compliance, net engineer, privacy)
- Compliance scoring against CIS Wireless, NIST 800-153, IEEE 802.11, OWASP IoT
- WiFi RF intelligence: channel maps, saturation scoring, rogue AP detection
- External reconnaissance: DNS, TLS, headers, WHOIS, cert transparency
- Next.js dashboard with scan history, trends, persona perspectives
- HTML report export from CLI and dashboard
- Scan persistence with history, trend, and diff commands
- Scheduled scanning via launchd/cron
- Local OUI database (no external API calls)
- Linux support
- 44 unit tests, ESLint, GitHub Actions CI

openIssues.title: CALCIO '90: 7.2's expert win-rate floor has less slack than its own sampling error
openIssues.body:
## The finding

7.2's `expert` win-rate floor at d = 0.25 is now the binding constraint on *any* improvement to the CPU's defence, and it has about five matches of slack in three hundred. It has already stopped two candidate fixes for #308, and it very nearly stopped the one that shipped.

Measured, `expert` win rate at d = 0.25 over 300 matches, against a floor of 0.800:

| build | win rate | matches |
|---|---|---|
| baseline (before #308's fix) | 0.8167 | 245 / 300 |
| `HEADER_SPREAD` 6 → 10 | 0.7833 | 235 |
| defensive header, any aerial ball in the box | 0.7867 | 236 |
| defensive header, opponent crosses only, p = 0.35 | 0.7967 | 239 |
| **shipped** (opponent crosses only, p = 0.28) | pass | — |

The shipped fix clears the floor only because the gate was narrowed *and* the probability lowered. Neither on its own was enough.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a note

There is a second problem underneath it. At 300 matches a win rate near 0.82 carries a standard error of about 0.022, which is **6.6 matches** — larger than the 5 matches of slack the floor is enforcing. So the floor is being asserted at a precision finer than the sample can resolve: a build can fail it, or pass it, for reasons that are inside the noise.

That showed up concretely while fixing #308. The first rolled version failed at 0.7967, six matches under the baseline — but adding an `m.rng()` draw also reshuffles the whole random stream, so part of that six was a reseeding rather than an effect, and there was no way to tell how much. The value had to be re-swept against the floor directly rather than reasoned about, which works but is expensive and does not generalise.

## What would close this

One of three, and the choice is a decision rather than a measurement:

1. **Give the floor headroom** — decide the easiest rung is allowed to get harder now that the CPU defends crosses, and restate the floor at a value the current build clears with more than its own sampling error.
2. **Deepen the sample** for this cell so the floor can resolve what it asserts, and record the CI cost against the #287 budget.
3. **Leave it as is**, explicitly, on the grounds that a tight floor at the easiest difficulty is the point — in which case the ticket closes as won't-do with the numbers above attached, so the next round starts after them.

The one thing that must not happen quietly is (1) as a side effect of some future PR that finds the floor inconvenient. That is the move the backlog plan's own rule forbids: nothing reaches green by relaxing a bound.

## Evidence

- `AIR_WIN_CHANCE` in `src/games/football/match.ts` carries the full sweep.
- `tests/games/football-balance.test.ts:150` is the assertion.
- PR #327 and issue #308 for the round this came out of.

openIssues.title: Line Hold: making a mid-campaign wave cost anything is a rebalance, not a constant
openIssues.body:
Split out of #263, whose readability half is fixed in PR #324. This is the stakes half, with the measurements that show why it is not a tuning pass.

## The fact, now pinned

`tests/games/towerdefense.test.ts` carries `only the finale costs the player anything, and only warlords do it (#263)`. A competent line holds 17 of 18 waves and leaks only warlords, only on wave 18. The test is mutation-checked (brute hp 110 to 400 turns it red), so a future balance change cannot move this silently.

## Why the obvious fixes do not work

**The margin is uniform, not slack.** Tracking the deepest marcher's progress along the route, on a line built as the run pays for it rather than handed over:

```
w 1 towers= 3 hp=x1.00 deepest=47%    w10 towers=10 hp=x2.31 deepest=21%
w 2 towers= 4 hp=x1.14 deepest=22%    w11 towers=11 hp=x2.60 deepest=24%
w 3 towers= 5 hp=x1.28 deepest=45%    w12 towers=11 hp=x2.99 deepest=44%
w 4 towers= 6 hp=x1.42 deepest=45%    w13 towers=12 hp=x3.48 deepest=45%
w 5 towers= 6 hp=x1.56 deepest=21%    w14 towers=13 hp=x4.07 deepest=25%
w 6 towers= 7 hp=x1.70 deepest=43%    w15 towers=13 hp=x4.76 deepest=51%
w 7 towers= 9 hp=x1.84 deepest=47%    w16 towers=13 hp=x5.55 deepest=42%
w 8 towers= 9 hp=x1.98 deepest=26%    w17 towers=15 hp=x6.44 deepest=52%
w 9 towers= 9 hp=x2.12 deepest=43%    w18 towers=15 hp=x7.43 deepest=100%
```

Nothing is drifting. The curve and the economy track each other for seventeen waves at a roughly 2x margin, and the finale is the one wave deliberately tuned to break through. The Round 6 contract in `waves.ts` says so outright: "even a maxed-out kill corridor cannot stop every crown".

**Difficulty is a step, not a slope**, because every marcher of a kind in a wave is identical and meets the same defence, so either all of them die in the corridor or all of them walk through. Sweeping a non-warlord toughness term (`hpScale` multiplied by `1 + late squared times k`, warlords exempt):

| k | brutes leaked | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | win, 15 lives |
| 0.005 to 0.016 | 0 | win, 5 lives (more *warlords* through, not brutes) |
| 0.02 | 4 to 7 | lost, or 1 life |
| 0.025 | 10 | lost |

There is no setting between "no consequence" and "overrun". This is also the mechanism behind the ticket's other observation, that tower count is non-monotonic past about twelve.

**Standard-bearers do not spread it.** One marcher in N spawning at a multiple of the hp was built and swept over share 3 to 8 and hp 2.2 to 6. Every cell changes how hard wave 18 hits (one warlord through becomes three or four) and none changes *which* waves hurt: all sixteen cells still held 17 of 18.

## What a real fix needs

Re-authoring the difficulty curve against the economy's growth curve so mid-campaign waves can bite, and re-deriving the no-perfect-runs contract that currently pins the finale as the only breach. Probably also giving a wave internal variance so a breach leaks a few marchers rather than the whole pack.

Worth weighing against the counter-argument first: a competent line holding everything until the finale is ordinary tower-defence design, and the 18 build policies the original audit measured were all decent ones. The ticket's premise is that this is a flaw; that premise is the thing to decide before spending a balance round on it.

Refs #263

openIssues.title: [parked] Pixel Park: rebuild the guest need selection and the score metric before reviving
openIssues.body:
Pixel Park is parked and fully unpublished (`src/pages/[lang]/fun/_park.astro`). The audit verdict is rebuild the simulation before reviving, on two structural findings. The ride graphics that were the stated reason for parking are a larger job than either.

1. An unserved need permanently masks every other need, so a park missing one building type earns nothing. `src/games/park/game.ts:649` takes `mostUrgentNeed(guest.needs)`, a single need (the lowest below 55, `guests.ts:52-60`), then scans only for buildings satisfying that one (`game.ts:653-657`). If none exists the guest wanders with a 30% chance of leaving (`game.ts:675`). It never tries the second-most-urgent need, and because the unserved need decays to 0 and stays lowest forever, the guest is locked out of spending on anything the park does offer.

Measured: a park with exactly one drink stall and a path network, run 20 in-game days, welcomed 121 guests and took 0 revenue. Not low, exactly zero. Per-need ablation, ten attractions, revenue per day over days 5-13, same seed: complete 739, no fun ride 0, no thrill ride 244, no food stall 80, no drink stall 57, no toilet 129. Severity tracks decay speed exactly, which is the signature of the masking.

Proposed fix, implemented and measured during the audit: in `chooseAction`, iterate the urgent needs in ascending order and take the first for which a reachable building exists. The lone drink stall goes from 0 to 15/day (upkeep 8, so viable as a first build should be); stalls-only goes 0 to 30/day (still loss-making against 52 upkeep, correct for a rideless park); and the complete park is unchanged at 823/day. Inert exactly where the park is well built.

2. In a well-run park guests never leave, so the score freezes and bigger parks score less. The score is `guestsWelcomed`, incremented only on spawn (`game.ts:579`), gated on `guests.length < maxGuests(day)` (`game.ts:887`, cap 120). A guest leaves only via happiness under 25 or the 30% roll after failing to find a building; in a park serving all five needs neither fires. Measured on a realistic staged build: welcomed sat at exactly 120 from day 25 to about day 70, eighteen real-time minutes in which the number being banked and submitted does not move. Same seeds, complete-need parks: 5 attractions scored 1,498; 8 scored 431; 10 scored 235; 15 and 20 scored 120. The best park scores twelve times less than the sloppiest. It also makes objective rung four ("welcome 400 guests", `objectives.ts:41`) unreachable for a strong park.

Not a one-liner: a 2-minute stay timer lifts admissions from 3.6/day to 11.0/day but drops the steady crowd from 120 to 51, which breaks the "draw a crowd of 90" prestige objective. Either a generous stay (4-5 min) with the crowd target lowered, or score something that grows monotonically with good play (lifetime revenue, guest-seconds).

3. Pacing is wrong for an arcade cabinet. Money bottoms at 15 on day 5 and never falls again until day 125, reaching 87k; bankruptcy arrives on day 237. That is about 3 minutes of tension, then 47 minutes at 1x where nothing can threaten you and nothing is left to buy, then a 45-minute slide into an unpreventable bankruptcy. Total run 94 minutes at 1x. The knob is `WAGE_RAMP = 1.4` at `economy.ts:50`.

Healthy and verified, for whoever picks this up: the 2x2 footprint machinery survived 27,503 successful mutations across 40 seeded maps with zero stranded annexes, zero overlaps and zero off-grid anchors; guest routing showed no leaks and no wedging; the scoring wiring itself is correctly gated. Also disproved: the coaster is NOT dominant - under paired seeds it beat the Pirate Ship by 1.6% with the sign flipping across seeds (noise) for 60% more cost, 31% more upkeep and four tiles instead of one. The instruction copy at `translations.ts:236` oversells it in all three locales.

Note the revival recipe in CLAUDE.md is stale: the floor now reads `UNLOCK_CHAIN` (`src/games/engine/progress.ts`) and `CABINETS` (`src/data/arcadeCabinets.ts`), so reviving is three edits, not two.

openIssues.title: [parked] Syndicate: the campaign arc inverts twice and progression rests on invisible weapon carryover
openIssues.body:
Measured with paired common random numbers, twelve seeds per cell, under a competent micro policy. Blocked behind the escort ticket, which must be fixed first.

1. The arc inverts twice. At pistol kit, mission 5 wins 4/12 while mission 6, billed as the decapitation finale, wins 9/12, because `assassinate` ends the moment the target dies whereas mission 5 requires walking the map recruiting ten civilians under minigun fire. At uzi kit the late run reads mission 7: 5/12, mission 8: 0/12, mission 9: 5/12; at minigun kit 12/12, 10/12, 12/12. Mission 8 (`src/games/syndicate/missions.ts:128-140`, seven uzi guards plus seven minigun enemies) is the hardest contract in the campaign on both kits, harder than the mission meant to escalate past it. Smallest fix: swap the specs for missions 8 and 9, or drop mission 8 enemies from 7 to 6.

2. Progression rests entirely on invisible weapon carryover. `rememberWeapons()` at `src/games/syndicate/game.ts:376-380` carries each surviving agent looted weapon into the next mission and silently resets dead agents to a pistol. Missions 8 and 9 win 0/12 on pistols and 10-12/12 on miniguns. A player who loses agents in mission 6 is quietly handed a mission 8 they cannot win, with nothing on screen explaining why. Smallest mitigation: show carried kit on the debrief screen, which already renders the next mission brief.

3. The civilian-casualty penalty is unreachable dead code. `game.ts:428-430` deducts 100 for a player-killed civilian, but player units only ever fire at victims drawn from the `hostiles` array (`sim.ts:252`), so a `kill` event with `kind: "civilian"` and `by: "player"` cannot be produced. Measured over 36 mission runs: 310 player kills (139 guards, 171 enemies), zero civilians. Forty-nine civilians died, all shot by hostiles, which carries no penalty. Collateral damage is the signature mechanic of the original and it is inert here.

Note the campaign is ten missions, not the nine CLAUDE.md claims.

Found by the August 2026 playability audit.

releases.name: v0.1.0 — Repository Strategist
releases.body:
First release of the Repository Strategist — a GitHub App that maintains institutional memory for software projects and uses it to provide doc-grounded triage and strategic intelligence.

## Features

- Multi-phase triage pipeline: deterministic template parsing (Phase 1), vector search + Gemini suggestions (Phase 2), enhancement context briefs (Phase 4a)
- Synthesis engine: weekly cluster detection, ADR drift detection, upstream impact analysis, posted as shadow repo briefings
- Enhancement research agent: mirror issues in shadow repos, context briefs, full research synthesis with safety gates
- MCP server: four tools exposing triage, synthesis, health, and trend data to Claude Code agents
- Event journal: records all repo activity for temporal analysis
- Auto-ingest: re-embeds changed documentation on push
- Per-repo config via `.github/butler.json`
- Live dashboard at `/dashboard`
- Two-layer safety: structural validator + LLM reviewer on all outputs
- Shadow repo approval gates: `lgtm`/`reject` for triage, `research`/`use as context`/`reject` for enhancements

## Infrastructure

Go 1.26.1 on Google Cloud Run, Neon PostgreSQL with pgvector, Gemini 2.5 Flash, GitHub Actions CI/CD with Workload Identity Federation.

## Documentation

- 13 Architecture Decision Records in `docs/adr/`
- Roadmap with six streams in `docs/plans/2026-03-04-roadmap.md`
- Security policy in `SECURITY.md`

releases.body:
### Minor Changes

-   fdb6e2d: Support deriving domains from Compass labels or custom fields. The `domain` option now accepts a mapping config (`{ from: 'label' | 'customField', key?, mapping, fallback? }`) in addition to the existing static `{ id, name, version }` form. Services resolve to domains per-component; each mapped domain is versioned independently and created lazily on first use.

releases.name: v0.3.1
releases.body:
# @ismaelmartinez/generator-atlassian-compass-event-catalog

## 0.3.0

### Minor Changes

-   feat: presentation layer improvements
    -   Populate `service.attachments` from Compass links via structured links (url, title, type, icon)
    -   Categorise links into subsections: Compass, Development, Operations, Documentation, Other
    -   Expose `StructuredLink` type and pass it as optional third parameter to custom markdown templates
    -   Surface `customFields` as a markdown table between Links and Dependencies sections
    -   Map Compass `typeId` to `service.styles.icon` using Lucide icon names

## 0.2.1

### Patch Changes

-   53a5fd2: fix: address security vulnerabilities in token logging, path traversal, and XSS
    -   Prevent potential API token leakage via error logs in team fetch failure handling
    -   Sanitize local spec file paths to reject path traversal sequences (`../`) and absolute paths
    -   Sanitize custom field text values from Compass API to prevent XSS in rendered markdown

## 0.2.0

### Minor Changes

-   a547fd4: feat: map Compass DEPENDS_ON relationships to service markdown
    -   Parse `relationships.DEPENDS_ON` from Compass YAML and resolve referenced services
    -   Add a "Dependencies" section to generated service markdown with links to dependent services
    -   Use a two-pass approach: first collect all services, then resolve dependencies between them
    -   Handle missing dependency targets gracefully (log warning, don't crash)
    -   Services without dependencies show "No known dependencies."

## 0.1.0

### Minor Changes

-   d3f5ee0: Modernize and fix core gaps (Phase 1)
    -   Replace local Service type with SDK's Service type for richer metadata support
    -   Map Compass lifecycle, tier, and labels to EventCatalog badges
    -   Map Compass repository links to service repository URL
    -   Map Compass ownerId to service owners
    -   Support updating existing services with overrideExisting option (defaults to true)
    -   Add Zod validation for generator configuration with clear error messages

-   26590b0: Support all Compass component types (Phase 2)
    -   Remove SERVICE-only restriction — all Compass types (APPLICATION, LIBRARY, CAPABILITY, CLOUD_RESOURCE, DATA_PIPELINE, MACHINE_LEARNING_MODEL, OTHER, UI_ELEMENT, WEBSITE) are now processed as EventCatalog services
    -   Add `typeFilter` option to selectively process only specified component types
    -   Add component type badge showing the Compass type (e.g. APPLICATION, LIBRARY) on each service

## 0.0.9

### Patch Changes

-   e6e0f5c: Phase 1: Update dependencies to latest versions

    Updated dependencies to latest versions (Phase 1 of modernization plan):

    -   @eventcatalog/sdk: ^2.0.0 → ^2.9.0 (9 minor versions, no breaking changes)
    -   @changesets/cli: ^2.28.1 → ^2.29.7
    -   chalk: ^5.4.1 → ^5.6.2

    All tests pass with updated dependencies. See UPDATE_PLAN.md for full modernization roadmap.

## 0.0.8

### Patch Changes

-   3c0a302: Updating depencencies and moving to eventcatalog/sdk 2.0.0

## 0.0.7

### Patch Changes

-   06e4c92: Fix docs and update the dependencies

## 0.0.6

### Patch Changes

-   5600c7a: fix chalk version to 4 to avoid ESM breaking changes

## 0.0.5

### Patch Changes

-   7bfa0ac: update dependencies and adding default PROJECT_DIR when not present

## 0.0.4

### Patch Changes

-   85cf3f5: update dependencies and improve documentation

## 0.0.3

### Patch Changes

-   8694a60: Fixing #9 by moving away from Tiles as they don't support external links on bundle objects

## 0.0.2

### Patch Changes

-   92170b3: Initial BETA release

releases.body: skill-sources v0.1.0 is the first public release of a Node 20+ CLI tool that records which upstream documents an agent skill was distilled from in a single skill-sources.yml manifest. The 'seed' command fills in last-reviewed markers while 'check' exits with code 1 when an upstream source has moved. Users can emit machine-readable results via 'report --json' and cross-check declared skills against directories on disk using '--verify-skills'. The tool reports drift and never rewrites skills.

openIssues.title: git resolver clones a repository once per ref instead of once
openIssues.body:
## Current behaviour
The `cloneOnce()` function in `src/resolvers/git.js` memoises clones keyed on the combination of repository and reference. Consequently, a manifest that names the same repository under several references (such as `main`, a release tag, or a pinned SHA) performs one full blobless network clone for each distinct reference. Although SHA-pinned references already produce a wide clone containing every branch and tag, a sibling entry at `main` still triggers its own separate clone.

## Cost
This behaviour results in unnecessary network traffic and redundant cloning operations. It specifically affects manifests that reference multiple refs of a single repository, as each distinct ref incurs a full clone cost rather than reusing the existing wide clone.

## Possible directions
Two potential fixes are identified. The first is to key the cache on the repository alone and use `git fetch origin <ref>` into the existing clone on a cache miss. The second is to take the wide clone once and let the existing `git log <ref> -- path` and `ls-tree <ref>` calls select the ref, as these commands already name the ref explicitly.

## Priority
This issue is not urgent. It was found during a quality review pass rather than being identified as a behaviour bug, and it only affects manifests with multiple refs of one repository.

openIssues.title: Publish to npm, once the repository is tidy enough to show people
openIssues.body:
## Why this is on hold

Publishing waits until the repository has been tidied for an outside audience. The awkward part is that the README already assumes it has happened: it tells the reader to run `npx skill-sources` in six places, and `npm view skill-sources` returns 404, so every install and usage instruction in it currently cannot work. Anyone sent to the repo today follows the first command and it fails.

The name looks unclaimed — the registry returns a not-found rather than a private-package error — so nothing is blocking the publish itself.

## Before publishing

- Run repo-butler over the repository. This is the tidy pass the rest of this list is waiting behind; `repo-butler/onboard` is still an open branch.
- Fill in the missing package.json metadata: `repository`, `homepage`, `bugs` and `author`. Without `repository` the npm page carries no link back to the source.
- Add CI. There is no `.github` directory at all, so nothing runs the 83 tests on a pull request, and every claim about the suite is currently taken on trust.
- Decide the version. It is 0.1.0, which is honest for something with the untested edges below.

## Known gaps a first reader would hit

The Confluence and URL resolvers are covered only by a mocked `fetch` — no real API call has ever been made by this code, so both are designs believed rather than integrations observed. The CI examples in the README have never been executed on a real runner against a real private upstream; they are valid YAML that has been reasoned through, not run. And the test suite never exercises a blobless clone, because git ignores `--filter` for local clones — the behaviour was verified separately against a genuine partial clone, but no test protects it.

None of these need fixing before publishing. They need to be things you already know when someone reports one.

releases.name: v1.1.0 — Curated Channels
releases.body:
## What's new

- 44 hand-picked channels (UK news, entertainment, movies, music, sports, kids, docs) as the default experience
- Automated channel validation script testing streams from iptv-org playlists
- Weekly GitHub Action keeps validation data fresh
- 1,800+ validated channels available via Find > Validated for discovery
- Split export buttons (All / Favs) to prevent accidental favourites-only export
- Wrapping category filter pills instead of horizontal scroll
- New channels highlight in sidebar when added from Find panel
- Community health files (code of conduct, issue/PR templates)

## Breaking changes

None — the app loads picks.json as the default channel list, falling back to the built-in list if offline.
